You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From d7a83d67a1694c42cc95fc0755d823f7ca3bfcfb Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Claudiu Beznea <claudiu.beznea@microchip.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Jan 2020 13:36:48 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] clk: at91: usb: use proper usbs_mask

Use usbs_mask passed as argument. The usbs_mask is different for
SAM9X60.

Fixes: 2423eeaead6f8 ("clk: at91: usb: Add sam9x60 support")
Signed-off-by: Claudiu Beznea <claudiu.beznea@microchip.com>
Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/1579261009-4573-4-git-send-email-claudiu.beznea@microchip.com
Acked-by: Alexandre Belloni <alexandre.belloni@bootlin.com>
Signed-off-by: Stephen Boyd <sboyd@kernel.org>
---
 drivers/clk/at91/clk-usb.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/drivers/clk/at91/clk-usb.c b/drivers/clk/at91/clk-usb.c
index 3c0bd7e51b09..c0895c993cce 100644
--- a/drivers/clk/at91/clk-usb.c
+++ b/drivers/clk/at91/clk-usb.c
@@ -214,7 +214,7 @@ _at91sam9x5_clk_register_usb(struct regmap *regmap, const char *name,
 
 	usb->hw.init = &init;
 	usb->regmap = regmap;
-	usb->usbs_mask = SAM9X5_USBS_MASK;
+	usb->usbs_mask = usbs_mask;
 
 	hw = &usb->hw;
 	ret = clk_hw_register(NULL, &usb->hw);
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by using a hardcoded `SAM9X5_USBS_MASK` instead of the appropriate `usbs_mask` that is passed as an argument. This oversight led to incorrect behavior when handling USB clocks for the SAM9X60, which requires a different mask than the SAM9X5.
